reviewed: all 14 ABI functions (owner, permittedCaller, Ownable, add/remove/checkPermittedCaller, supportsInterface, TuringRandom, Turing42, TuringTx, GetResponse, GetRandom, Get42)

findings.issue: GetErrorCode's twelve messages are built at constant offsets but merged through five phi variables per nesting level into a single raw revert, so the reasons appear only as hex words ('0x545552494e473a20496e73756666696369656e7420...' for 'TURING: Insufficient credit'); GetResponse prints the same logic as twelve decoded 'revert with ...' lines.
findings.rule: Do not merge reverts whose data differ only in a constant string; keep one revert per path (or sink the revert into each arm) so the Error(string) can be decoded, and print printable 32-byte words as strings.
findings.verified: by reading: 0x545552494e473a20496e73756666696369656e74206372656469740000000000 is ASCII 'TURING: Insufficient credit' (length 27)

findings.issue: Two ceil32 terms of the call's argument layout are merged into '2 * Mask(250, 5, x + 31)'.

notes: No loops in TuringHelper.sol (source_loops 0); the six text whiles are memory copies (P7). Permitted-caller checks, Self calls with (1, url, payload), (1, 0) and (2, 42), event arguments, GetResponse's checks and the early revert per error code match the source. No immutables.
summary: All 14 functions reviewed; no source loops and the semantics match. GetRandom and Get42 hide GetErrorCode's messages behind a 12-level phi chain and one raw revert, unlike GetResponse where the same messages are decoded.
